correctness.rationale: The exact order-statistic probability mass is P(M=k)=F_k(p)^m-F_(k-1)(p)^m, with F the Bin(n,p) CDF. At n=2, the quadratic discriminant is q^(2m)*([(1-p)^m+(1+p)^m]^2-4)>0 by strict convexity for m>=2, and all coefficients are positive, so the roots are strictly negative. For any fixed n>=3,m>=2, coefficientwise convergence of G(t/p) at p->0 gives m(1+t)^n-(m-1) with a simple nonreal zero; fixed-degree root continuity supplies a genuine positive-p failure interval. For n=3,m=2, exact sympy re-expansion of the CDF squared verifies Disc_z G=108 p^6(1-p)^12 Q(p), Q=4p^6+8p^3+3p^2+6p-1. Q increases strictly from -1 to 20 and has a unique positive root; positive PGF coefficients exclude nonnegative real roots, so sign of the discriminant yields the precise iff. At equality its simple discriminant zero implies exactly one double negative root. Crosschecks verify polynomial factorization and sampled signs; the universal n>=3 statement uses analytic root continuity, not a finite grid.
residual_risks: Independent bounded experiments are supplementary; no formal Lean theorem or external expert attestation is asserted.
